Integrated view with Beige Book:

- FOMC (Jan 26, 2022): Activity and employment continued to strengthen; inflation elevated; policy pivot toward tightening (ending net asset purchases by early March and preparing to raise rates).
- Beige Book (early Jan 2022 reference): Most Districts reported modest-to-moderate growth, but the Omicron outbreak weighed on in-person services, with noted sales impacts in leisure/hospitality. Labor markets remained very tight with strong wage growth, and price pressures were broad-based as firms passed through higher input costs. Supply chain bottlenecks persisted. Outlook remained positive but marked by virus and inflation uncertainty.
- SLOOS overlay: Easier C&I standards and stronger business loan demand support near-term activity; however, softer residential mortgage demand and expected deterioration in some household credit segments as rates rise temper the upside.

Net: Conditions remain modestly positive, supported by solid business demand and ongoing expansion, but tempered by Omicron-related disruptions, persistent supply/labor constraints, and elevated inflation. Adjusting for Beige Book headwinds, the stance shifts slightly less positive than the prior 0.20.
